lines: A history of long and effortless success can be a dreadful handicap, but, if properly handled, it may become a driving force. When the United States entered just such a glowing period after the end of the Second World War, it had a market eight times larger than any competitor, giving its industries unparalleled economies of scale. Its scientists were the world's best; its workers the most skilled. America and Americans were prosperous beyond the dreams of the Europeans and Asians whose economies the war had destroyed.
长期不费吹灰之力获得成功的历史可能成为一种可怕的障碍，但若处理得当，它也可能转化为一种推动力。二战结束后，美国恰好进入了这样一个辉煌时期：它拥有比任何竞争者大八倍的市场，使其工业享有无与伦比的规模经济。它的科学家是世界上最优秀的，它的工人是最熟练的。美国的繁荣与美国人的富足，是那些经济遭到战争破坏的欧亚诸国做梦也想不到的。

lines: It was inevitable that this primacy should have narrowed as other countries grew richer. Just as inevitably, the retreat from predominance proved painful. By the mid-1980s Americans had found themselves at a loss over their fading industrial competitiveness. Some huge American industries, such as consumer electronics, had shrunk or vanished in the face of foreign competition. By 1987 there was only one American television maker left, Zenith. (Now there is none: Zenith was bought by South Korea's LG Electronics in July.) Foreign-made cars and textiles were sweeping into the domestic market. America's machine-tool industry was on the ropes. For a while it looked as though the making of semiconductors, which America had invented and which sat at the heart of the new computer age, was going to be the next casualty.

随着其他国家日益富裕，美国的这种领先优势不可避免地缩小了。同样不可避免的是，失去主导地位的过程令人痛苦。到20世纪80年代中期，美国人已对本国日渐减弱的工业竞争力感到不知所措。面对外国竞争，美国一些规模庞大的产业，如消费电子业，已经萎缩或消失。到1987年，美国只剩下一家电视机制造商——增你智。（如今一家也没有了：增你智已于7月被韩国 LG 电子公司收购。）外国制造的汽车和纺织品正大量涌入美国国内市场。美国的机床工业已濒临困境。有一段时间，半导体制造业似乎将成为下一个受害者；半导体是美国发明的，也是新计算机时代的核心。

lines: All of this caused a **crisis** of confidence. Americans stopped taking prosperity for granted. They began to believe that their way of doing business was failing, and that their incomes would therefore shortly begin to fall as well. The mid-1980s brought one inquiry after another into the causes of America's industrial decline. Their sometimes sensational findings were filled with warnings about the growing competition from overseas.
这一切引发了信心危机。美国人不再把繁荣视作理所当然。他们开始相信自己的经商方式正在失灵，他们的收入也将因此很快开始下降。80年代中期，人们对美国工业衰退的原因进行了一次又一次的调查。调查结果有时耸人听闻，其中充满了对日益增长的海外竞争的警告。

lines: How things have changed! In 1995 the United States can look back on five years of solid growth while Japan has been struggling. Few Americans attribute this solely to such obvious causes as a devalued dollar or the turning of the business cycle. Self-doubt has yielded to blind **pride**. 'American industry has changed its structure, has gone on a diet, has learnt to be more quick-witted,' according to Richard Cavanagh, executive dean of Harvard's Kennedy School of Government. 'It makes me proud to be an American just to see how our businesses are improving their productivity,' says Stephen Moore of the Cato Institute, a think-tank in Washington, DC. And William Sahlman of the Harvard Business School believes that people will look back on this period as 'a golden age of business management in the United States.'

世事变化真快！1995年，美国可以回顾五大年头的稳固增长，而日本却一直在苦苦挣扎。很少有美国人把这一切仅仅归因于美元贬值或商业周期的转折这样显而易见的原因。自我怀疑已被盲目骄傲所取代。哈佛大学肯尼迪管理学院执行院长理查德·卡佛纳说：“美国的工业已经改变了结构，精简了机构，学会了更加机智灵活。”位于华盛顿特区的智囊团——卡托研究所的斯蒂芬·莫尔说：“看到我们的企业不断提高生产率，作为一个美国人，我感到自豪。”哈佛商学院的威廉·萨尔曼则认为，人们将来回顾这段时期时，会把它视为“美国企业管理的黄金时代”。

lines: Being a man has always been dangerous. There are about 105 males born for every 100 females, but this ratio drops to near balance at the age of **maturity**, and among 70-year-olds there are twice as many women as men. But the great universal of male mortality is being changed. Now, boy babies survive almost as well as girls do. This means that, for the first time, there will be an excess of boys in those crucial years when they are searching for a mate. More important, another chance for natural selection has been removed. Fifty years ago, the chance of a baby (particularly a boy baby) surviving depended on its weight. A kilogram too light or too heavy meant almost certain death. Today it makes almost no difference. Since much of the variation is due to genes, one more agent of evolution has gone.

身为男性，一直以来都伴随着风险。每出生100名女婴，大约就有105名男婴，但到成年时，这一比例便降至接近平衡；而在70岁的人群中，女性人数是男性的两倍。不过，男性死亡率较高这一普遍现象正在改变。如今，男婴的存活情况几乎和女婴一样好。这意味着，在寻找伴侣的那些关键年份，男性人数将首次出现过剩。更重要的是，自然选择的又一次机会被消除了。五十年前，婴儿，尤其是男婴，能否存活取决于其体重。体重过轻或过重一公斤，几乎就意味着必死无疑。如今，体重几乎不再造成差别。由于这些差异在很大程度上源于基因，进化的又一个驱动因素消失了。

lines: There is another way to commit evolutionary suicide: stay alive, but have fewer children. Few people are as fertile as in the past. Except in some religious communities, very few women have 15 children. Nowadays the number of births, like the age of death, has become average. Most of us have roughly the same number of offspring. Again, differences between people and the opportunity for natural selection to take advantage of it have diminished. India shows what is happening. The country offers wealth for a few in the great cities and poverty for the remaining tribal peoples. The grand mediocrity of today—everyone being the same in survival and number of offspring—means that natural selection has lost 80% of its power in upper-middle-class India compared to the tribes.

还有一种在进化意义上自我毁灭的方式：活下来，但少生孩子。如今，很少有人像过去那样多生育了。除某些宗教社群外，几乎没有女性会生15个孩子。如今，生育子女的数量就像死亡年龄一样，变得趋于一致。我们大多数人的子女数量大致相同。人与人之间的差异，以及自然选择利用这种差异的机会，再一次减少了。印度的情况说明了正在发生的变化。这个国家让大城市中的少数人享有财富，却让其余的部落居民生活在贫困之中。如今这种普遍的平均化——每个人的存活情况和子女数量都相同——意味着，与部落人群相比，自然选择在印度中上层人群中的作用已减弱了80%。

lines: For us, this means that evolution is over; the biological Utopia has arrived. Strangely, it has involved little physical change. No other species fills so many places in nature. But in the past 100,000 years—even the past 100 years—our lives have been transformed but our bodies have not. We did not evolve, because machines and society did it for us. Darwin had a phrase to describe those ignorant of evolution: they 'look at an organic being as a savage looks at a ship, as at something wholly beyond his comprehension.' No doubt we will remember a 20th century way of life beyond comprehension for its ugliness. But however amazed our descendants may be at how far from Utopia we were, they will look just like us.

对我们而言，这意味着进化已经终结：生物学上的乌托邦已经到来。奇怪的是，这一过程几乎没有带来身体上的变化。没有哪个物种像人类这样在自然界中占据如此多的空间。但在过去的十万年——乃至过去的一百年间——我们的生活已被改变，而我们的身体却未曾改变。我们没有进化，因为机器和社会替我们完成了进化。达尔文曾用一句话描述对进化无知的人：他们“看待一个有机生命体，如同野人看待一条船，把它当作完全超出自己理解力的东西”。毫无疑问，我们会记住20世纪的生活方式，其丑陋之处难以言表。但是，无论我们的后代对我们离乌托邦之遥远感到多么惊讶，他们的长相都将与我们如出一辙。

lines: When a new movement in art attains a certain fashion, it is advisable to find out what its advocates are aiming at, for, however farfetched and unreasonable their principles may seem today, it is possible that in years to come they may be regarded as normal. With regard to Futurist poetry, however, the case is rather difficult, for whatever Futurist poetry may be—even admitting that the theory on which it is based may be right—it can hardly be classed as Literature.
当一种新的艺术运动形成某种时尚时，明智的做法是弄清其倡导者的目标所在，因为无论其主张在今天看来多么牵强附会、荒诞不经，将来人们却可能视之为常态。然而，就未来主义诗歌而言，情况却颇为棘手：因为无论未来主义诗歌为何物——即便承认其赖以立足的理论可能正确——它也很难被归入文学的范畴。

lines: This, in brief, is what the Futurist says: for a century, past conditions of life have been conditionally speeding up, till now we live in a world of noise and violence and speed. Consequently, our feelings, thoughts and emotions have undergone a corresponding change. This speeding up of life, says the Futurist, requires a new form of expression. We must speed up our literature too, if we want to interpret modern stress. We must pour out a large stream of essential words, unhampered by stops, or qualifying adjectives, or finite verbs. Instead of describing sounds we must make up words that imitate them; we must use many sizes of type and different colored inks on the same page, and shorten or lengthen words at will.

简言之，未来主义者的主张是：一个世纪以来，过去的生活状况一直在有条件地加速，直到今天我们生活在一个充满喧嚣、暴力和速度的世界里。因此，我们的感觉、思想和情感也经历了相应的变化。未来主义者说，生活的加速需要一种新的表达形式。如果我们想诠释现代生活的种种压力，就必须同样加快文学的步伐。我们必须倾泻出大量基本词汇，不受标点符号、修饰性形容词或限定动词的束缚。我们不去描绘声音，而要造出模仿声音的词语；必须在同一页纸上使用多种字号和不同颜色的墨水，随意缩短或拉长单词。

lines: Certainly their descriptions of battles are confused. But it is a little upsetting to read in the explanatory notes that a certain line describes a fight between a Turkish and a Bulgarian officer on a bridge off which they both fall into the river—and then to find that the line consists of the noise of their falling and the weights of the officers: 'Pluff! Pluff! A hundred and eighty-five kilograms.' This, though it fulfills the laws and requirements of Futurist poetry, can hardly be classed as Literature. All the same, no thinking man can refuse to accept their first proposition: that a great change in our emotional life calls for a change of expression. The whole question is really this: have we essentially changed?

他们对战斗的描写当然是混乱的。但是，先在注解中读到，某行诗描写一名土耳其军官与一名保加利亚军官在桥上打斗，随后双双掉进河里，再发现这行诗居然只是两人落水的声音和他们的体重：“扑通！扑通！一百八十五公斤。”——这确实有些令人不快。这样的诗句虽然符合未来派诗歌的规则和要求，却很难称得上文学。尽管如此，任何有思想的人都不能拒绝接受他们的第一个主张：情感生活的巨大变化，需要表达方式随之改变。问题的关键其实是：我们在本质上发生变化了吗？

lines: Aimlessness has hardly been typical of the postwar Japan whose productivity and social harmony are the envy of the United States and Europe. But increasingly the Japanese are seeing a decline of the traditional work-moral values. Ten years ago young people were hardworking and saw their jobs as their primary reason for being, but now Japan has largely fulfilled its economic needs, and young people don't know where they should go next.

'Those things that do not show up in the test scores—personality, ability, courage or humanity—are completely ignored,' says Toshiki Kaifu, chairman of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party's education committee. 'Frustration against this kind of thing leads kids to drop out and run wild.' Last year Japan experienced 2,125 incidents of school violence, including 929 assaults on teachers. Amid the outcry, many conservative leaders are seeking a return to the prewar emphasis on moral education. Last year Mitsuo Setoyama, who was then education minister, raised eyebrows when he argued that liberal reforms introduced by the American occupation authorities after World War II had weakened the 'Japanese morality of respect for parents.'

lines: But that may have more to do with Japanese life-styles. 'In Japan,' says educator Yoko Muro, 'it's never a question of whether you enjoy your job and your life, but only how much you can endure.' With economic growth has come centralization; fully 76 percent of Japan's 119 million citizens live in cities where community and the extended family have been abandoned in favor of isolated, two-generation households. Urban Japanese have long endured lengthy commutes (travels to and from work) and crowded living conditions, but as the old group and family values weaken, the discomfort is beginning to tell. In the past decade, the Japanese divorce rate, while still well below that of the United States, has increased by more than 50 percent, and suicides have increased by nearly one-quarter.

lines: If ambition is to be well regarded, the rewards of ambition—wealth, distinction, control over one's destiny—must be deemed worthy of the sacrifices made on ambition's behalf. If the tradition of ambition is to have vitality, it must be widely shared; and it especially must be highly regarded by people who are themselves admired, the educated not least among them. In an odd way, however, it is the educated who have claimed to have given up on ambition as an ideal. What is odd is that they have perhaps most benefited from ambition—if not always their own then that of their parents and grandparents. There is a heavy note of hypocrisy in this, a case of closing the barn door after the horses have escaped—with the educated themselves riding on them.

如果人们能正确看待抱负，那么它带来的回报——财富、名望以及对自己命运的掌控——就必须被视为值得为之付出的牺牲。如果雄心壮志的传统要焕发活力，它就必须得到广泛的推崇；尤其必须受到那些本身令人敬慕的人士的高度重视，而受过教育者当属其中之要。然而，恰恰是那些受过教育的人诡异地宣称，他们已经把抱负从理想中放弃了。奇怪的是，他们恰恰可能是从抱负中受益最多的人——如果不是受益于他们自身的抱负，便是受益于他们父母和祖辈的抱负。这里面含有浓厚的虚伪色彩，好比马厩里的马跑光了才去关门——而受过教育的人自己正骑在那些马背上。

lines: Certainly people do not seem less interested in success and its signs now than formerly. Summer homes, European travel, BMWs—the locations, place names and name brands may change, but such items do not seem less in demand today than a decade or two years ago. What has happened is that people cannot confess fully to their dreams, as easily and openly as once they could, lest they be thought pushing, acquisitive and vulgar. Instead, we are treated to fine hypocritical spectacles, which now more than ever seem in ample supply: the critic of American materialism with a Southampton summer home; the publisher of radical books who takes his meals in three-star restaurants; the journalist advocating participatory democracy in all phases of life, whose own children are enrolled in private schools. For such people and many more perhaps not so exceptional, the proper formulation is, 'Succeed at all costs but avoid appearing ambitious.'

当然，如今人们对成功及其标志的兴趣似乎并未逊于从前。避暑别墅、欧洲旅行、宝马汽车——地点、地名和品牌也许会变化，但如今人们对这些东西的需求似乎并不比十年前或两年前少。所发生变化的是，人们已不能像从前那样轻松坦然地坦陈自己的梦想，唯恐被人认为爱出风头、贪得无厌、庸俗不堪。相反，我们目睹了种种精美的虚伪景观，它们如今比以往任何时候都似乎俯拾皆是：批评美国物质主义的评论家在南安普顿拥有避暑别墅；出版激进书籍的出版商在三星级餐厅用餐；鼓吹生活各领域皆应实行参与式民主的记者，其子女却就读于私立学校。对这类人以及更多或许不那么出格的人而言，恰切的表述是：“不惜一切代价取得成功，但不要让人看出你有野心。”

lines: The attacks on ambition are many and come from various angles; its public defenders are few and unimpressive, where they are not extremely unattractive. As a result, the support for ambition as a healthy impulse, a quality to be admired and fixed in the mind of the young, is probably lower than it has ever been in the United States. This does not mean that ambition is at an end, that people no longer feel its stirrings and promptings, but only that, no longer openly honored, it is less openly professed. Consequences follow from this, of course, some of which are that ambition is driven underground, or made sly. Such, then, is the way things stand: on the left angry critics, on the right stupid supporters, and in the middle, as usual, the majority of earnest people trying to get on in life.

对抱负的攻击为数众多，且来自方方面面；而为之公开辩护者却寥寥无几、平淡无奇，甚至说不上有什么吸引力。结果，把抱负视为一种健康的动力、一种理应受到仰慕并铭刻于青年心灵的品质来加以支持的程度，在美国也许已降至有史以来的最低点。这并不意味着抱负已经穷途末路——人们不再感受到它的涌动与激励——而只是意味着，由于不再受到公开的推崇，人们也就不那么公开地宣示它了。由此当然会产生种种后果，其中之一便是抱负被赶入地下，或变得诡诈隐蔽。于是，时下的局面便是：左面是愤怒的批评者，右面是愚拙的支持者，而居中的，一如既往，是大多数努力在人生道路上进取的真诚之人。

lines: Governments throughout the world act on the assumption that the welfare of their people depends largely on the economic strength and wealth of the community. Under modern conditions, this requires varying measures of centralized control and hence the help of specialized scientists such as economists and operational research experts. Furthermore, it is obvious that the strength of a country's economy is directly bound up with the efficiency of its agriculture and industry, and that this in turn rests upon the efforts of scientists and technologists of all kinds. It also means that governments are increasingly compelled to interfere in these sectors in order to step up production and ensure that it is utilized to the best advantage. For example, they may encourage research in various ways, including the setting up of their own research centers; they may alter the structure of education, or interfere in order to reduce the wastage of natural resources or tap resources hitherto unexploited; or they may cooperate directly in the growing number of international projects related to science, economics and industry. In any case, all such interventions are heavily dependent on scientific advice and also scientific and technological manpower of all kinds.

世界各国政府都基于这样一种假设行事：人民的福利在很大程度上取决于本社会的经济实力与财富。在现代条件下，这就需要不同程度的集中控制，从而也就需要获得诸如经济学家和运筹学专家等各类专门科学家的帮助。再者，显而易见的是，一个国家的经济实力与其工农业生产效率直接相关，而效率的提高又有赖于各类科技人员的努力。这同时意味着，各国政府正日益被迫介入这些部门，以便提高生产并确保生产得到最有效的利用。例如，政府可以用种种方式鼓励研究，包括建立自己的研究中心；可以改变教育结构，或进行干预以减少自然资源的浪费、开发迄今尚未利用的资源；还可以在日益增多的与科学、经济和工业有关的国际项目中直接进行合作。但无论如何，这一切干预都极大地依赖于科学咨询，也依赖于各类科技人才。

lines: Owing to the remarkable development in mass-communications, people everywhere are feeling new wants and are being exposed to new customs and ideas, while governments are often forced to introduce still further innovations for the reasons given above. At the same time, the normal rate of social change throughout the world is taking place at a vastly accelerated speed compared with the past. For example, in the early industrialized countries of Europe the process of industrialization—with all the far-reaching changes in social patterns that followed—was spread over nearly a century, whereas nowadays a developing nation may undergo the same process in a decade or so. All this has the effect of building up unusual pressures and tensions within the community and consequently presents serious problems for the governments concerned. Additional social stresses may also occur because of the population explosion or problems arising from mass migration movements—themselves made relatively easy nowadays by modern means of transport. As a result of all these factors, governments are becoming increasingly dependent on biologists and social scientists for planning the appropriate programs and putting them into effect.

由于大众通信的迅猛发展，各地的人们正不断感到有新的需求，并不断接触到新的习俗和思想；而基于上述种种原因，各国政府也常常被迫推行更进一步的革新。与此同时，与过去相比，世界各地社会变化的常规速度正在大大加快。例如，在早期实现工业化的欧洲国家中，工业化进程——以及随之而来的社会模式的各种深刻变革——延续了将近一个世纪，而如今一个发展中国家可能在十年左右的时间里就走完同样的过程。这一切造成的结果是：社会内部积聚起异乎寻常的压力和紧张，从而给有关政府带来了严重的问题。此外，人口爆炸或大规模移民潮所引发的问题也会造成额外的社会压力——如今现代交通工具的发达本身已使大规模移民相对容易。由于所有这些因素，各国政府在规划适当的方案并付诸实施时，正越来越依赖于生物学家和社会科学家。

data.chart_note: 两幅对比图：上图'1900年，一艘渔船，网中鱼满为患，海面上鱼群密布'；下图'1995年，渔船林立，网中几乎无鱼，茫茫大海只有一条小鱼'。图题：A Brief History of World Commercial Fishing。
sample: The two pictures present a striking contrast in the history of world commercial fishing. In 1900, a single fishing boat went out to sea, and the ocean abounded with all kinds of fish; the fishermen, with only a simple net, could easily catch a big haul of fish. By 1995, however, fishing boats had multiplied, and with much more advanced equipment they struggled to catch fish, yet the sea seemed almost empty—only one small fish could be seen in their net.
这两幅图形成了世界商业捕鱼史上一个触目惊心的对比。1900年，一条渔船出海，海中鱼类资源丰富，渔民只需一张简陋的渔网，便可轻易满载而归。然而到了1995年，渔船成倍增加，渔民虽然配备了先进得多的设备，捕鱼却已十分艰难，大海几乎空空如也——网上只见一条小鱼。

sample: The painter's purpose is not difficult to perceive: he wants to warn us that excessive commercial fishing and mankind's blind pursuit of economic profit have exhausted the fishery resources of the ocean. If this trend continues, not only will fish disappear from the world, but the ecological balance of the sea will be destroyed, and human beings themselves will eventually suffer from the catastrophe they have caused.
画者的用意不难领会：他意在警示我们，过度的商业捕捞和人类对经济利润的盲目追逐，已经使海洋渔业资源趋于枯竭。如果这一趋势继续下去，不仅鱼类将从世界上消失，海洋的生态平衡也将遭到破坏，人类自己最终也将深受其害。

sample: Therefore, effective counter-measures must be taken immediately. First, the government should make strict laws to limit the fishing season and the number of fishing boats, and prohibit the use of fine nets that trap young fish. Second, more artificial breeding farms should be set up to release young fish into the sea. Third, people all over the world should be made to realize the importance of protecting marine resources. Only when fishing is carried out in a rational and sustainable way can we keep the ocean an inexhaustible treasure for generations to come.
因此，必须立即采取有效的对策。第一，政府应制定严格的法律，限制捕捞季节和渔船数量，禁止使用捕捞幼鱼的细密渔网。第二，应建立更多的人工养殖场，向大海放流鱼苗。第三，应使全世界的人们认识到保护海洋资源的重要性。只有以合理、可持续的方式进行捕捞，我们才能让海洋成为子孙后代取之不尽的宝藏。
